title: PROFILE-DEVIATION-CERT: does the (model, anchor) deviation term carry certifiable content beyond the global theta? (zero judge calls; plan A1)
question: Every published profile row is theta_ac = theta_a + delta_ac on the anchor's own board, and the record has never published delta_ac with a certificate of its own. Does delta_ac carry certifiable content beyond theta_m, i.e. for some (model, anchor) cells may the record say 'm is certified above / below its own standing in anchor c'? The cell is the ANCHOR (sub-anchor rows closed twice).

the registered judge deviation delta_ac = theta_ac(per-anchor MM, prior 0.5) - theta_m(pooled MM, prior 0.5) is biased by construction: the Jeffreys prior is ~190 pseudo-matches against 695-2,881 real matches per anchor but 21,536 pooled, so under the exact null delta_hat ~ -(1 - k_pool/k_anchor) * theta_m; measured slope -0.2185 (r -0.761); under a null on the real schedule 129/140 = 92.1% of anchor families carry >= 1 false certificate at nominal 5% (synthetic 80.7%). READING OF RECORD: the PRIOR-MATCHED deviation delta'_ac (pooled prior scaled by pooled / anchor matches; null family rate 2.9% real / 3.6% synthetic); the registered reading printed beside every count and not scored; (c) and C1 unchanged; a certified SIGN is preserved, a magnitude is not published; profile_deviation_cert.py amended before --run.

plain_description.what: For each model and subject anchor, it tests whether the model's subject-specific deviation from its overall strength can be certified, using either the key or the judge. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: Per-cell profiles are only informative if "model X is certainly better or worse than usual here" can be stated. This checks whether such statements are supported.
plain_description.information: If the judge's certified deviations agree with the key, profiles add real per-cell content. Result: the judge certified 22 of 280 cells, but 3 of these (13.6%) have the wrong sign against an established key. That triggers the registered rule (a count rule, not a significance claim). The certified set is not confirmed by the key. No 'above or below its own standing' claim is published for any judge-built cell, and profiles stay a re-indexed global score. Older judged question family, later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
